root.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Bogoljubow Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 a6 5. e4

overview: Black plays 4...a6 and after 5.e4 b5 6.e5 Nd5 7.a4 the game turns on tactics against White's queenside and the advanced e5 pawn. Black has the c4 pawn and plans ...e6, ...Bb7 and ...Nxc3, while White fights with a4, Ng5 and Be2 for the initiative. Theory is deep and the lines are forcing.

white_ideas.idea: Hit the b5 pawn with a4 and open lines on the queenside
Use the e5 pawn to restrict Black and attack with Ng5 and Qg4

black_ideas.idea: Support the b5 pawn with ...c6 or ...Bb7, and trade the central knights with ...Nxc3
Develop with ...e6 and ...Be7, keeping the pawn on c4

typical_structures.structure: White e5 spearhead and open queenside
Black c4/b5 pawns against White a4

character.notes: Both sides take risks, with the extra pawn on c4 and attacks on the queenside and the e5 pawn.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn is the normal QGA pawn, which White can regain, so it is not a deliberate gambit.

soundness.notes: Sound for both sides; the main line is well studied.

structure.notes: The e-pawn spearhead and open files give an open centre.

approach.notes: Played by strong players in the QGA.

level.notes: Long forcing lines need to be known.

character.reason: Forcing lines with e5, a4 and ...b5 give both sides real risks.

gambit.reason: The c4 pawn is the QGA pawn, which White can regain.

structure.reason: The e5 spearhead and open queenside make an open centre.

level.reason: The forcing theory around 7.a4 has to be learned.

plans.reason: White gains space with e5 and both sides fight on the queenside with a4 and ...b5.
